text:
IncidentBot: Paging on-call: Dedicated capacity p99 latency breach detected for region-us-west-2 — auto-escalation to on-call-eng. Alerts: p95=420ms p99=2.3s streaming stalls increased 8x, queue depth > 1200.

oncall-amber: I'm on it. seeing the same in dashboards, p99 spike started ~1766667700. attaching traces.

sarah.ops: customers reporting streaming stalls and truncated responses. CS Triage: Tom, any impacted customers with active tickets?

tom-customer-success: Customer-A reported degraded interactive chat, timeouts around 10-15s on their side. Open ticket #INC-3321.

mike.ml: Quick look at pool metrics — dedicated-pool-7 showing 100% GPU utilization, handshake success dropping to 68%, warmup queue growing. autoscaler logs show scale-up requested at 1766667718, but new slots didn't register until 1766667780. handshake drift between scheduler and pool.

jia.eng: logs: ```
[1766667718] autoscaler: scale_request(pool=dedicated-pool-7, delta=4)
[1766667720] pool-manager: allocate_slots -> initiating warmup
[1766667745] pool-heartbeat: slot-12 warmup: pending (kv-cache-miss)
[1766667770] scheduler: handshake timeout for slot-13
[1766667780] pool-manager: slot-12 registered
[1766667782] autoscaler: scale_ack delayed
```

ops-lead: That warmup delay looks like KV cache cold path + image pull latency on new nodes. Are these hotshot instances with prewarmed images?

mike.ml: They were supposed to be prewarmed (hotshot=enabled) but recent rollout changed base image tag -> longer container startup. We rolled a minor runtime tweak yesterday. Could be correlated.

oncall-amber: Mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily increase per-pool burst_capacity until handshake stabilizes. 2) Route new incoming requests to fallback model-variant (smaller) to reduce pressure. 3) Notify CS of temporary rate limits per-customer if needed. I'll execute 1 now.

IncidentBot: ops command executed by oncall-amber: `/pool burst-capacity add dedicated-pool-7 3 --ttl 15m` — success.

sarah.ops: Throttling applied at edge to heavy customers: Customer-A reduced to 60% of prior rate to avoid hard timeouts.

mike.ml: After burst-capacity bump, queue depth dropped from 1.2k -> 420 in ~30s. p95 down to ~210ms. p99 falling but still elevated ~950ms. Streaming stall errors reduced but not gone.

jia.eng: Still seeing streaming tail spikes for requests with long context. Traces show repeated KV-cache cold-path resolutions causing token emission stuttering. Example trace snippet: ```
emit(0..64): stable
emit(65..128): stall 1200ms (kv cache fill)
emit(129..): stable
```

ops-lead: For longer-term, we should: a) rollback the runtime image tweak causing slower warmup, or b) bake image with prepopulated kv-cache snapshot for hotshot nodes. Which is faster?

mike.ml: Rollback is fastest to restore prior warmup times. I'll prepare a rollback PR and coordinate. But rollback takes ~15m to cut and roll across pools — risk incremental churn. Alternative is to increase prewarmed replica counts for pools temporarily.

oncall-amber: Can we do a partial routing rule: route streaming requests with context > 4k to model-variant-small that doesn't require heavy KV usage? That would reduce tail load.

sarah.ops: We pushed a routing override for contexts > 4k -> variant-lite. IncidentBot: routing change applied.

mike.ml: Nice — immediate drop in long-tail tokens. p99 now ~560ms. Still some customers see transient errors while warmups finish.

tom-customer-success: Update to Customer-A: we applied temporary rate limiting and routing to a smaller model-variant, which should reduce timeouts. They acknowledged and will monitor.

jia.eng: Monitoring handshake metrics: handshake_success increased from 68% -> 91% after burst bump + routing change. Warmup queue now stable under 200.

ops-lead: Good. Next steps: 1) Mike to open rollback PR for runtime image tag and include postmortem checklist. 2) Jia to add a prewarm healthcheck to detect KV-cache cold misses on slot registration. 3) Sarah/Tom to follow up with impacted customers and confirm recovery. 4) Add autoscaler backoff tuning to avoid delayed ack misinterpretation.

mike.ml: I'll open PR and tag eng-runtime for review. ETA 25m for PR, 45m for canary rollback once approved.

oncall-amber: I'll stay on page for the next 60m and coordinate handoff to next oncall at 1766668120. If p99 holds < 700ms for 10m, we'll declare mitigated.

IncidentBot: Pager note: Mitigation in progress. p99 trending down. Escalation paused.

sarah.ops: Quick note for postmortem: include customer impact window, number of affected requests, warmup delay root cause (image change + kv-cache cold path), and action items (rollback, prewarm snapshot, autoscaler ack handling).

ops-lead: Agreed. Also add a runbook update: when handshake_success < 80% trigger burst-capacity auto-bump and route long-context requests to variant-lite.

tom-customer-success: Customer-A confirmed reduced timeouts and said UX acceptable for now. We'll keep them updated.

oncall-amber: Handoff: next oncall @oncall-amber -> @sarah.ops at 1766668120. Leaving a pinned note with actions in the incident doc.

IncidentBot: Thread closed for now, will re-open if metrics regress.
